description: The workbench page is a remote origin (http://127.0.0.1:<kernel port>), so Tauri's ACL denies its invokes by default. Grant only what the injected workbench scripts actually call — plus one caller nobody writes in this repo: tauri-plugin-opener injects its own click interceptor (init-iife.js, open_js_links_on_click defaults to true) into EVERY webview, and it calls plugin:opener|open_url on any `<a target="_blank">` / Ctrl-click without a .catch (2026-10-15: the kernel renders conversation links exactly that way, so one click produced an unhandled rejection, harness-health.js reported it as a workbench fault, and guard.rs then mis-attributed it to the kernel). `opener:allow-default-urls` is required alongside `opener:allow-open-url` because that command validates the URL scope itself (tauri-plugin-opener src/commands.rs): granting the command alone turns the ACL refusal into a ForbiddenUrl error — the same denial in different words. `opener:default` is deliberately NOT used: it would also bring allow-reveal-item-in-dir, which the workbench page has no use for. This does not widen what the shell already does — on_new_window hands http(s) to the system browser anyway. The wildcard port covers the release/debug defaults (3090/3091) and any custom port in settings.json; the origin is still pinned to loopback and the harness window.
